page: Vultr vx1-m-96c-768gb is a high-capacity instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring 96 dedicated AMD vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. This memory-to-CPU ratio positions the instance as a memory-optimized resource suitable for handling large datasets in memory.

A key architectural tradeoff of this instance is its local storage configuration. The server includes only 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, which is insufficient for primary data storage and necessitates the use of external or network-attached storage volumes for operational workloads. The instance also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature any GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-m-96c-768gb offers high resource density, combining a massive dedicated AMD core count with a substantial memory footprint on a single virtual machine. This configuration is designed for workloads that require significant memory capacity and parallel processing power without the need for local high-capacity storage. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, heavy data processing pipelines, and memory-intensive analytics.
